svg.title: P001 · Brand directory
svg.desc: One row per usable brand. Products 1 and 2 both become Nike. On 5, removing three spaces leaves an empty string. IDs 3, 4 and 5 drop out. The five remaining products still include repeated brands. The five values form three groups. Nike appears twice, Adidas twice and Puma once. Alphabetical ordering gives Adidas, Nike and Puma. Each name appears once.
svg.text: Will product 2 create a second Nike entry if the stored name has spaces?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Dots inside quotes show padding. SQL excerpts use … for omitted
Products 1 and 2 both become Nike. On 5, removing three spaces leaves an empty string.
Which product rows can supply a brand?
IDs 3, 4 and 5 drop out. The five remaining products still include repeated brands.
WHERE TRIM(Brand) IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(Brand)) > 0
The five values form three groups. Nike appears twice, Adidas twice and Puma once.
How should the filter list read?
Alphabetical ordering gives Adidas, Nike and Puma. Each name appears once.
